tasks.name: Vertical Lines (Easy)
tasks.Instructions:
To improve your drawing skills, it's essential to first develop strong hand-eye coordination.
One of the simplest and most effective ways to do this is by practicing basic shapes and lines.

Trace these lines as closely as you can and make sure you only use a single stroke per line.

tasks.name: Horizontal Lines (medium)
tasks.Instructions:
Trace these lines as closely as you can. Watch out for the straightness of your lines!

Tip: For short lines, keep your fingers relaxed and draw using wrist movement, keeping your hand position stable.

tasks.name: Vertical Lines (Medium)
tasks.Instructions:
Trace these lines as closely as you can. Watch out for the straightness of your lines!

Tip: To keep long lines straight, lock your wrist and fingers and draw from your elbow or shoulder.

tasks.name: Horizontal Lines (hard)
tasks.Instructions:
Trace these lines as closely as you can. Watch out for the straightness of your lines!

Tip: If you make a mistake, just undo the line using the button above your canvas and try again - accuracy improves with repetition!

tasks.name: Angled Lines (Easy)
tasks.Instructions:
Trace these lines as closely as you can. Watch out for the straightness of your lines!

Tip: With diagonal lines try to experiment with different hand positions and orientations to find what works for you best.

tasks.name: Angled Lines (Easy)
tasks.Instructions:
Trace these lines as closely as you can. Watch out for the straightness of your lines!

Tip: If you're struggling with a certain angle and just can't seem to get it right, try rotating your tablet/paper.

tasks.name: Angled Lines (Medium)
tasks.Instructions:
Trace these lines as closely as you can. Watch out for the straightness of your lines!

Tip: Before touching the canvas, hover your pen over the line and rehearse the motion a few times to get better results faster.

tasks.name: Angled Lines (Medium)
tasks.Instructions:
Trace these lines as closely as you can. Watch out for the straightness of your lines!

Tip: To improve muscle memory and prepare for all situations, practice drawing the lines in both directions (top->bottom and bottom->top).

tasks.name: Changing Direction (Easy)
tasks.Instructions:
Trace these lines as closely as you can.

Tip: Draw these in a single stroke to get used to directional changes while drawing.

tasks.name: Zig Zag (Hard)
tasks.Instructions:
Trace this line as closely as you can.

Tip: Try to make it in as little strokes as possible.

tasks.name: Vertical Paralell Lines
tasks.Instructions:
In this part of the lesson you will see pairs of dots. Place your pen on the first dot, look at the second one and connect them with a single line.

Tip: For better results keep your eyes focused on the second dot while drawing.

tasks.name: Horizontal Paralell Lines
tasks.Instructions:
Draw paralell lines according to the example.
Tip: Avoid stopping or correcting mid-line. A single, continuous stroke will produce a better result then multiple small adjustments.

tasks.name: Angled Paralell Lines
tasks.Instructions:
Draw paralell lines according to the example.
Tip: Try to stop exactly at the target dot - control at the end of the stroke is just as important as the start.

tasks.name: Angled Paralell Lines
tasks.Instructions:
Draw paralell lines according to the example.
 Tip: If you struggle with a certain orientation, make sure to return and repeat the exercise until it's not a problem anymore. Consistence is key!

tasks.name: Cube
tasks.Instructions:
One of the most important skills for an artist is understanding three-dimensional space.
The following exercises will help you become more comfortable drawing objects with depth and form. Do your best!

tasks.name: Pyramid
tasks.Instructions:
Trace the shown object as accurately as possible.

Tip: While drawing try to imagine where all the lines you don't see or only see partially will go. Watch out for paralel lines as well!

tasks.name: Cylinder
tasks.Instructions:
Trace the shown object as accurately as possible.

Tip: Symetrical shapes are easier to imagine and draw correctly.

tasks.Instructions: Trace the shown object as accurately as possible.

tasks.name: Simple Perspective With One Vanishing Point
tasks.Instructions:
While drawing in perspective, parallel lines appear to converge toward specific points in the distance.
These points are called vanishing points and they help create the illusion of depth and space on a flat surface.
In this course, we will focus on cases with one or two vanishing points.

In this exercise, you are provided with a grid template and a reference photo in the bottom-left corner. Your task is to trace the image onto the grid as accurately as possible.

tasks.name: Perspective With One Vanishing Point
tasks.Instructions:
Try to trace the image onto the grid as accurately as possible.

Tip: pay close attention to distance between different objects on the reference photo and how far they are from grid lines.

tasks.name: Hard Perspective With One Vanishing Point
tasks.Instructions:
Try to trace the image onto the grid as accurately as possible.

Tip: All horizontal lines are paralel.

tasks.name: Perspective With Two Vanishing Points
tasks.Instructions: Try to trace the image onto the grid as accurately as possible.
